focus: sk-create-figjam, manual-testing-playbook and the vendored mcp packages: registration drift, broken references and stale examples

findingDetails.title: The vendored chrome-devtools package documents two manuals the Product Owner config never registers, so every parallel-instance scenario cites a manual that does not exist
findingDetails.scopeProof: Every cited file is inside the declared review target; .utcp_config.json was read whole (4 manual_call_templates, none named chrome_devtools_1/_2/_3), and both vendored claims were read at the cited lines.
findingDetails.case: An operator runs the dual-instance-parallel scenario; it calls chrome_devtools_1.navigate and chrome_devtools_2.navigate, no manual with either name is registered, both calls error and the scenario reports FAIL against a product defect that does not exist.
findingDetails.claim: The vendored chrome-devtools README and manual asset describe an isolated multi-manual registration in .utcp_config.json that the Product Owner config does not contain.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Searched for a second config carrying the missing manuals; checked .mcp.json and opencode.json for chrome_devtools_1/2; checked whether README is framed as example rather than fact (both lines use indicative present tense).
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The vendored package is a byte-identical copy of the upstream Skilled packet and upstream's reference deployment registers the isolated pair; the single-live-manual config is a deliberate post-vendor simplification, making the drift a docs problem rather than a config problem.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if a Product Owner config outside the declared target registers chrome_devtools_1/2, or if the parallel-instance scenarios resolve manual names from the package asset file rather than from .utcp_config.json.

findingDetails.title: Code Mode registration mixes a pinned package with a floating @latest and an unversioned remote fetch, so the reviewed artifact is not the one that runs
findingDetails.scopeProof: .utcp_config.json read whole; all four manual_call_templates inspected and chrome-devtools-mcp@0.26.0 confirmed as the only pinned argument in the file.
findingDetails.case: figma-developer-mcp publishes a breaking rename of get_figma_data between two runs of the same reviewed release; nothing in the repository changes, gates still pass against the vendored copy, and the live manual no longer exposes the tool the catalog calls.
findingDetails.claim: Two of the four manual templates resolve an unpinned package at runtime while the rest of the system pins by version and base_commit.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Searched for a pin of figma-developer-mcp anywhere in the target; found none. Checked whether @latest is justified in mcp-figma docs; found no statement.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Floating tags may be deliberate for third-party servers whose vendors recommend @latest, trading reproducibility for freshness.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to non-finding if mcp-figma documents a deliberate @latest policy, or if the manual is version-pinned elsewhere in the system.

noveltyJustification: Both findings are new to the registry: no prior iteration examined .utcp_config.json manual registration, and the two open P1s concern the hub ROUTER.md rule and the format-validator fork. All six severity-weighted points this iteration are new.
